items.question: What substance should be recognized as the nectar that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: A specific substance is to be known as nectar
That nectar has a destructive effect on wrinkles
That nectar has a destructive effect on gray hair
items.inference: The substance in question is to be identified as the nectar that removes wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: One should know that as nectar, the destroyer of wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What bodily condition results from the practice described in this teaching?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair
The practitioner becomes devoid of all diseases
Both freedoms characterize the same resulting state
items.inference: The practice yields a body free from wrinkles, gray hair, and all diseases.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and devoid of all diseases.

items.question: Where should the tongue be applied to bring about the destruction of disease?
premises: The tongue is the instrument to be applied
The place of application is the root of the palate
The purpose of this application is the destruction of disease
items.inference: Applying the tongue at the root of the palate serves to destroy disease.
items.plain_english: One should indeed apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.

items.question: How should the tongue be positioned and maintained within one's own mouth?
premises: The tongue should be contracted
This contraction should be maintained always
The tongue should be united with one's own mouth
items.inference: The practitioner should constantly keep the tongue contracted and united within the mouth.
items.plain_english: One should always contract the tongue, keeping it united within one's own mouth.

items.question: What mental placement leads the practitioner to attain the state of unmanatā?
premises: The mind is to be placed in the heart
This placement is maintained until a certain state is reached
The goal is the attainment of unmanatā
items.inference: Fixing the mind in the heart leads to the attainment of the transcendent state of unmanatā.
items.plain_english: Placing the mind in the heart, one continues until reaching the state of unmanatā.

items.question: What well-guarded secret concerning time is now being revealed to the goddess?
premises: The subject is the deception of time
This knowledge was well guarded
This knowledge has now been made manifest
items.inference: The previously well-guarded secret of deceiving time is now revealed.
items.plain_english: O goddess, the well-guarded deception of time has now been made manifest.

items.question: Which chapter concludes as having issued forth from the moon island?
premises: The text refers to a chapter
It is identified as the sixth chapter

items.inference: The sixth chapter, issued forth from the moon island, concludes here.
uncertainties: candra-dvīpa may be a proper name or symbolic location
items.plain_english: The sixth chapter, issued forth from the Moon Island, is concluded.

items.question: What teaching about the three principles is requested by one who has taken sole refuge in the lord?
premises: The speaker requests instruction on the three principles
The speaker addresses the lord
The speaker has taken refuge in the lord alone
items.inference: Having taken sole refuge in the lord, the speaker asks to be taught the three principles.
items.plain_english: Tell me of the three principles, O lord; I have taken refuge in you alone.

items.question: How should what is present in the goddess's wheel be contemplated in relation to the moon?
premises: Something in the goddess's wheel is to be contemplated
The contemplation uses a comparison to the moon
The comparison refers to the moon on the first lunar day
items.inference: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel as one contemplates the moon on the first lunar day.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel, like the moon on the first day of the lunar fortnight.

items.question: Where is the crest said to be absorbed within the subtle body, O beautiful-faced one?
premises: The crest is the element absorbed
The absorption occurs in that location
The specific locus is the bone wheel
items.inference: The crest is absorbed there in the bone wheel.
uncertainties: asthi-cakre may refer to a specific subtle center
items.plain_english: And there indeed, O beautiful-faced one, the crest is absorbed in the bone wheel.

items.question: What qualities characterize the form that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: The form is accompanied by fluid
The form is black in appearance
This form destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: A fluid, black form is identified as the destroyer of wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: It is a fluid, black form, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What kind of yoga should be applied at the location of the base and support?

uncertainties: ādhāra-skandha-saṃsthāne may refer to a specific anatomical or subtle locus
items.plain_english: One should apply the cooling yoga at the location of the base and support.

items.question: How should the sun and the moon be regarded within this yogic practice?
premises: The sun should be seen as an enemy
The moon should be seen as a friend

items.inference: The practitioner should regard the sun as hostile and the moon as friendly.
items.plain_english: One should see the sun as an enemy and indeed see the moon as a friend.

items.question: What kind of physical location is suitable for undertaking this practice?

items.inference: A suitable place for practice is a solitary earthen house free from gnats and mosquitoes.
items.plain_english: In a solitary earthen house, in a secluded place free from gnats and mosquitoes.

items.plain_english: In a secluded, deserted, divine place adorned with multitudes of flowers.

items.question: What level of attainment is realized after six months of this practice?
premises: A period of six months is specified
Perfection becomes known after this period
This perfection is equal to the state of a yoginī
items.inference: After six months, one attains a perfection equal to the state of a yoginī.
items.plain_english: After six months, perfection is known, equal to the state of a yoginī.

items.question: What threefold reality is situated at the brahma knot, O beautiful-faced one?
premises: Something is situated at the brahma knot
The teaching refers to three entities
The goddess is addressed directly
items.inference: Three entities are indeed situated at the brahma knot.
uncertainties: The referent of etāṃ and trīṇi is unclear without broader context
items.plain_english: Situated at the brahma knot, O beautiful-faced one, these are indeed the three.

items.question: What should be colored with the fluid, including even the pores of the body?

The entire body should be colored

items.inference: One should color the whole body, beginning with the pores, with the fluid.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should color everything, beginning with the pores, with the fluid.

items.question: Within what timeframe is the promised result certain to occur without doubt?

There is no doubt about this result
The timeframe is within six months
items.inference: The result will certainly occur within six months.
items.plain_english: It indeed comes to pass without doubt, within six months.

premises: The form is accompanied by fluid
The form is black in color

items.question: What rejuvenating transformation occurs through six months of repeated practice?
premises: The practice is performed for six months
The practice is repeated and sustained

items.question: What dark-colored reality is encountered upon resorting to the place of the yoginī?

items.question: What ultimate freedom from decay and affliction is attained through this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from old age and death
The practitioner becomes devoid of disease and illness

items.plain_english: One becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
